reason: The hypothesis relies on specific claims about Ti–Cu intermetallic formation, wetting improvement, and composite performance, but the cited evidence (E1, E2) only discusses oxygen/nitrogen effects on phase stability in a Ti-V-Nb-Ta alloy and does not address W–Cu systems, Ti coatings, SPS, or interfacial bonding. No prior evidence is provided for any of the key premises.
premises: A thin Ti coating on W particles can be deposited uniformly by vapor deposition.
During SPS, the Ti coating reacts with Cu to form an interfacial Ti–Cu intermetallic compound.
The Ti–Cu intermetallic improves wetting and bonding between W and Cu.
Improved wetting and bonding reduces void formation and phase separation in the W–Cu composite.
The resulting composite has superior thermal transport and mechanical durability under irradiation.
